common_name: Nectar Ninja Hyssop (Compact Rounded Pollinator-Magnet Hyssop)

planting.note: Set container plants in average to poor, well-drained soil in full sun; good air movement around the naturally rounded habit helps prevent mildew.

directions: This Walters Gardens introduction forms a dense, naturally rounded mound of green foliage that holds its shape without shearing. Soft lavender-blue flower spikes cover the plant from midsummer into late summer and draw heavy bee and pollinator traffic, living up to the cultivar name. Grow it in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun, since rich or damp conditions promote lankiness and mildew. Once established it tolerates drought well and only needs a post-bloom trim to keep its bushy form tidy.

common_name: Rise and Shine Citrus Sunrise Red Hot Poker (Golden-Yellow Wide-Leaved Torch Lily)

planting.note: Plant in hot, well-drained soil in full sun; in zones 4-6 tie the foliage up over the crown in autumn to shed excess moisture and avoid winter rot.

directions: Part of the Rise and Shine series Walters Gardens is releasing, Citrus Sunrise sends up golden-yellow flower spikes well above a clump of noticeably wider, lusher grass-like leaves than older red hot poker varieties. Expect a strong early-summer flush with reliable rebloom carrying color into late summer. It wants hot, dry, sharply drained soil and full sun, and is evergreen in mild climates but dies back to the crown where winters are harsh. Hummingbirds and butterflies visit the torch-like blooms heavily, and the clump is both deer- and rabbit-resistant once established.

common_name: Rise and Shine Mango Mimosa Red Hot Poker (Copper-Orange Dark-Bud Torch Lily)

planting.note: Plant in hot, well-drained soil in full sun; trim leaf tips in spring to refresh growth and, in zones 4-6, bundle foliage over the crown before winter.

directions: Mango Mimosa is the companion Rise and Shine release alongside Citrus Sunrise, opening copper-orange flowers from dark buds on spikes that rise above wide, lush, grass-like foliage. It blooms slightly earlier and stays a touch shorter and tighter than its sibling, with the same strong rebloom extending color through summer. Give it hot, dry, well-drained sites in full sun, since soggy winter crowns are its main vulnerability in colder zones. Established clumps are drought tolerant, deer- and rabbit-resistant, and reliably attract hummingbirds and butterflies to the torch-shaped blooms.

common_name: Glowing Reviews Mountain Fleece (Golden-Foliage Cerise-Red Fall-Blooming Persicaria)

planting.note: Plant in consistently moist, well-drained soil (clay-tolerant) in full sun to part shade; keep watered through dry spells to prevent leaf stress.

directions: Glowing Reviews pairs golden chartreuse foliage that resists burning in full sun with vibrant cerise-red flower spikes that emerge from dark red buds in early fall, extending garden color later in the season than most perennials. It blooms earlier and grows more vigorously than the industry-standard 'Golden Arrows' selection. Grow it in evenly moist, well-drained soil, including clay, and keep it watered during dry stretches since mountain fleece performs best without drought stress. Once established it is long-lived, deer- and rabbit-resistant, and the colorful spikes work well as late-season cut flowers.

common_name: Art and Sol Purple People Eater Mangave (Blue-Green Rosette with Reddish-Purple Spotting)

planting.note: Plant in sharply drained, dry-to-average soil in full sun after frost danger passes; in cold climates grow in containers and overwinter dry and above 60°F.

directions: Purple People Eater forms a neat rosette of thick, blue-green leaves heavily spotted in reddish-purple, giving the whole plant a purple cast from a distance that intensifies with full-sun exposure. Upward-curving leaf margins carry yellow, orange, and cinnamon-brown spines tipped in cinnamon at each leaf point. As an Agave x Manfreda hybrid it combines Manfreda vigor with Agave structure, growing well in containers or dry landscape beds. Water and fertilize lightly during active summer growth, then keep it nearly dry over winter and protected from temperatures below 60°F where it is not hardy.

common_name: Sun Jewels Pink Diamonds Bleeding Heart (Two-Tone Pink Full-Sun Alpine Dicentra)

planting.note: Plant in full sun in sharply drained, average-moisture soil; unlike woodland bleeding hearts this alpine type declines in wet or heavy clay sites.

directions: Pink Diamonds belongs to the Sun Jewels series of alpine bleeding hearts that break with tradition by thriving in full sun rather than shade. Two-tone pink flowers open light pink and deepen with age, blooming from late spring through early summer and continuing intermittently into fall above fine, fern-like blue-green foliage. Because it comes from high-elevation alpine stock rather than woodland species, it needs excellent drainage and resents soggy or heavy clay soil, which causes yellowing and decline. Established plants are deer resistant and draw hummingbirds and bees over an unusually long bloom season for a Dicentra.

common_name: Urophysa (Columbine-Leaved Rock Garden Perennial, Winter White Blooms)

planting.note: Tuck small plants into a sharply drained rock-garden pocket or dry overhang in light shade; soggy winter soil is its main killer, not cold.

directions: A rarely cultivated Chinese relative of columbine, Urophysa henryi forms a tight evergreen clump of lacy, columbine-like foliage only a few inches tall. From January through March it produces clusters of small outfacing white flowers, a welcome bloom window in the depths of winter. It wants light shade and sharp drainage, performing best tucked under a dry overhang where winter rain can't pool around the crown. Established plants shrug off cold to at least 11°F, making drainage the limiting factor rather than hardiness.

common_name: Lisann Hellebore (Abundant Outfacing White Winter Blooms)

planting.note: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade in fall, in a spot where the evergreen clump can stay undisturbed for years.

directions: A cross between Helleborus niger and H. x hybridus, 'Lisann' produces pure white, outward-facing flowers in far greater quantity and with better presentation than straight niger clones. The evergreen foliage stays attractive through winter and spring bloom season. Site it in part sun to light shade in soil that drains well but doesn't dry out completely, and leave it undisturbed since hellebores resent frequent transplanting. Its deer resistance and dry-shade tolerance suit it to a mixed woodland border.

common_name: Raspberry Wren Bugleweed (Golden Foliage, Rich Pink Spring Blooms)

planting.note: Space plugs or small pots about 15 inches apart in part sun to light shade for quick groundcover fill-in.

directions: Bred by Chris Hansen, this bugleweed pairs bright golden evergreen foliage with dense spikes of rich pink flowers in early spring, an unusually bold color combination for the genus. It spreads quickly into a flat groundcover mat in part sun to light shade. Once established it handles dry shade without supplemental watering, making it a low-upkeep filler under trees or along path edges. Deer tend to leave it alone, and it draws pollinators and hummingbirds while in bloom.
